messages.text: Start the importer, and ask me whatever you need.
Four things to settle before I write any of it.

parts.question: Which database should the importer write to?

options.label: Postgres
options.description: A server, a schema and a migration to run before the first import.

options.label: SQLite
options.description: One file beside the worktree, no server to keep alive.

messages.text: Noted. The schema goes in first, then the reader.

parts.question: What should the importer call a row it cannot parse?

options.label: Rejected
options.description: The row is kept aside with its reason.

options.label: Skipped
options.description: The row is counted and dropped.

parts.answer: quarantined, and kept with the line number so I can read them later

messages.text: Quarantined it is. That needs a table of its own.

parts.question: Which formats should the first version read?

options.label: CSV
options.description: Comma separated, with a header row.

options.label: Excel
options.description: A workbook, one sheet per table.

parts.question: How large a file does it have to survive?

options.label: Up to a gigabyte
options.description: Stream it, and checkpoint as it goes.

parts.question: What should it do when the file is unreadable halfway through?

options.label: Stop and keep what landed
options.description: The import is left half done, and says where it stopped.

options.label: Roll the whole import back
options.description: Nothing lands unless all of it does.

messages.text: That is everything I had. One last thing before I start.

parts.question: Should the importer run on a schedule once it works?

options.label: Every night
options.description: A scheduled run at three, with a report in the morning.
